math_event.note: Final independent review passed P1=P2=P3=0 for the cellular-complex unit and its source corrections.

proof_repair_check.evidence: For r>=n+1 and n>k, r>k+1, so the relative groups in degrees k+1 and k both vanish and adjacent skeleta induce H_k-isomorphisms. Closure-finiteness plus weak topology proves that a compact subset lies in a finite subcomplex. Cycle support gives surjectivity; the joint support of a cycle and a bounding chain gives injectivity. The proof does not invoke cellular homology.

math_event.note: Final independent review passed P1=P2=P3=0 for the cellular-complex unit and its source corrections.

proof_repair_check.evidence: The composition d_n=rho_{n-1}delta_n is typed, and delta_{n-1}rho_{n-1}=0 is the consecutive-map relation in the long exact sequence. Vanishing above skeletal dimension makes rho_n and rho_{n-1} injective, giving ker d_n=im rho_n; rho_0 is the identity and d_0=0. The pair (X^(n+1),X^n), followed by FOM-PR-13, identifies cellular and singular homology. Maps of skeletal pairs prove naturality for cellular maps, and cellular approximation gives the arbitrary-continuous-map statement.

proof_repair_check.evidence: Both incidence spheres have dimension n-1, P_beta collapses precisely the summands delta!=beta, and the outward-normal-first boundary orientation introduces no hidden sign. Coordinate projection after the connecting map yields the stated degree coefficient. The n=1 endpoint incidence is correctly read in reduced H_0(S^0), and compactness of the attaching sphere gives finite support even when the CW complex has infinitely many cells.
